subject: Endgame account flagging & finance readout — EMEA Q2
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T08:12:00Z
Subject: Endgame account flagging & finance readout — EMEA Q2

Team —

We need a concise rollup for the EMEA endgame cohort ahead of Friday's finance readout. I pulled the raw endgame extract and attached it (EMEA_endgame_raw.csv). Please do the following by EOD Wednesday (2028-04-13):

- Owners: verify stage and committed ARR for each row you own. If the account is not true "endgame" (no active buyer execs + no procurement timeline), mark it OUT.
- Probability: adjust to the most defensible number (no optimistic hand-waving).
- Blockers: one-line note (pricing, legal, procurement, POC, other).
- Special handling: flag any accounts requiring finance credits, SLA exceptions, or unusual contract language.

I will compile a cleansed list for finance and execs by Thu morning. Key context: finance will treat anything not validated as a non-commit. We need precision here to avoid downstream surprises.

Attachments: [EMEA_endgame_raw.csv (6 KB)]

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T10:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Endgame account flagging & finance readout — EMEA Q2

Irene — thanks for the call to action. Quick notes for owners:

- I went through my book and am marking three accounts OUT: two stalled at procurement, one lost to competitor (we have the email thread).
- Flagged Acme Corp as HIGH RISK — procurement has an active pricing hold and there's an outstanding legal redline for data residency. I'm looping Sarah at Acme here; procurement@acme.com has been unresponsive to our last two notes.

Inline summary (owners):
- ACME — owner: marissa.cole — claimed ARR 210k, currently should be treated at 20% until procurement confirms.
- Deltan Ltd — owner: marissa.cole — OUT (procurement stalled >60d).
- Rhea Systems — owner: marissa.cole — OUT (signed competitor PO).

Attachment: ACME_Pricing_Negotiation.pdf (redlines from their counsel).

On Wed I'll upload a clean CSV to the shared Drive for Irene to ingest.

Marissa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Quick update —

- I reviewed the top 12 EMEA endgame rows assigned to me. Two moves to OUT (no buyer engagement for 75+ days). One account (Nexa Health) had procurement confirm verbal okay but legal needs a clause change — probability set to 60%.
- I've uploaded a cleaned file to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bEMEA-Endgame-Readout (EMEA_endgame_clean.csv) — Irene, use that for the readout import.

Small ask: Marissa, for ACME can you confirm whether the data-residency redline is a showstopper? If so, we should mark it OUT and avoid an inflated commit number.

Karthik
Head of EMEA Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa / Irene —

Thanks for the transparency. Quick update from our side: procurement has pushed pricing review to next Wednesday due to an internal budget cycle. Legal is still working the data-residency language; they can agree to a scoped residency clause but need a small addendum (their counsel shared comments — I attached them to this reply).

Practically speaking: procurement will not sign this week. We do expect movement next week after the pricing review. If you want to be conservative for the finance readout, treat the 210k as a 20% probability this week; I will update you if procurement moves it earlier.

Attachment: ACME_Legal_Comments_redlined.docx (45 KB)

—Sarah
Sarah Brock
Director, Strategic Procurement
Acme Corp
